events.title: Death of Augustus, First Roman Emperor
events.description: Augustus died in Nola at age 75, after ruling Rome for more than four decades. His stepson Tiberius succeeded him as emperor.
events.significance: Augustus's death marked the first transfer of imperial power in Rome and tested the stability of the Principate he had founded, which shaped Roman government for centuries.

events.title: France Announces the Daguerreotype
events.description: The French government announced the daguerreotype process, invented by Louis Daguerre, and made it freely available to the world, apart from in Britain.
events.significance: The announcement is widely regarded as the birth of practical photography and led to the rapid global spread of photographic imaging. World Photography Day is celebrated on this date.

events.title: Afghanistan Gains Independence from British Influence
events.description: The Treaty of Rawalpindi was signed, ending the Third Anglo-Afghan War. Britain recognized Afghanistan's right to conduct its own foreign affairs under Amir Amanullah Khan.
events.significance: The treaty restored full Afghan sovereignty in foreign policy, and Afghanistan celebrates the date as its Independence Day.

events.title: Trial of Francis Gary Powers
events.description: Soviet authorities convicted American U-2 pilot Francis Gary Powers of espionage after his spy plane was shot down over the USSR in May 1960. He was sentenced to ten years of confinement.
events.significance: The incident heightened Cold War tensions, derailed US-Soviet diplomacy, and ended in a 1962 prisoner exchange for Soviet spy Rudolf Abel.

events.title: Start of the Soviet Coup Attempt
events.description: Hardline Communist officials placed Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev under house arrest in Crimea and declared a state of emergency in an attempt to seize power. Boris Yeltsin rallied public resistance in Moscow.
events.significance: The coup collapsed within days, discrediting the Communist Party and accelerating the dissolution of the Soviet Union later in 1991.
